grf.initial_hypothesis: The v1 package-index mode-loss seam is the primary blocker.
grf.counter_reality_1: A source-hash-bound reparse can preserve syntax intent even if a discovery index is lossy.
grf.observed_v1_collapse: Merged v1 did hash-bound reparse, so mode-loss alone did not prove semantic corruption.
grf.counter_reality_2: Reparse still overclaims semantics if plain use is assumed to denote an exact module.
grf.discriminator: Compare universal exact-module treatment with canonical parser contract and authorized corpus.
grf.observed_result: Parser says UseDecl carries no resolution semantics, and authorized corpus contains symbol-shaped plain use frank.entity.Frank against module frank.entity + entity Frank.
grf.candidate_evolution: PR #674 subsequently removed the v1 seam by introducing ClayPackageIndex/v2 with ordered use_decls bound into package identity and ClayPackageResolution/v2 that consumes the indexed intent without a second source read.
grf.collapse: PROMOTE v2 lossless package-index provenance as the preferred candidate representation; REJECT universal exact-module semantics for plain MODULE-mode uses; RETAIN fail-closed plain-use semantics until an explicit reviewed name-binding contract exists.

external_primary_comparison.rust_reference: Name resolution is a distinct compiler process; use declarations are resolved and ambiguities are validated; Rust has explicit namespaces.
external_primary_comparison.go_spec: Imports explicitly name packages and qualified identifiers access exported identifiers; Go's rule is language-defined rather than inferred from path shape.
external_primary_comparison.clay_inheritance: NONE; these mechanisms demonstrate that import/name semantics require explicit language contracts, not that Clay should copy Rust or Go.
